chapter_theme: Having devotion (பக்தியுடைமை): the Lord, whom the seven worlds cannot know, is known only through the devotion of his devotees; the poet takes on servitude to the servants of his servants, calls to the Lord as a calf calls, and finds that in bondage and release alike the devotee has no task of his own, for grace does all.

2623.reading: The devotees praise as Pasupati the Father who stands as the knowledge that grants release and as what is heard, the undying Lord of the immortals, the pure one, the light that stands as the pure path.
2623.nuance: பசுபதி (Lord of the pasus, the bound souls) names the Siddhanta relation of Pati to pasu. கேள்வி is learning by hearing, here the teaching heard from the guru or scripture.

2624.reading: I took on the servitude of being servant to the servants of the servants of his servants; by the grace of the devotees, so that I might reach his feet, he took me as his servant, saying 'this one is my servant'.
2624.nuance: The repeated அடியார் stacks degrees of humility, a common form in Tamil Saiva hymns. The grace that brings the poet to the Lord comes through the devotees (அடியார் அருளால்), not directly.

2625.reading: He is cool in water and burns in fire; who can know Nandi? He is subtler than anyone one could find in the world, and he stands in the town as Uma's consort.
2625.nuance: Line 2, ஆரிக் கடனந்தி யாமா ரறிபவர், is hard to divide; it may be ஆர் இக்கடன் (who [knows] this duty) or a question about who can know Nandi. நேரியர் may mean subtle or upright. The verse sets the Lord's pervading power beside his form with Uma.

2626.reading: Who can say where the Father dwells, the One whom all seven worlds together cannot know? Unless one comes to share in the devotion of his devotees, who could speak of that pearl? Those who did stood first.
2626.nuance: முத்து (pearl) is a name for the Lord. The last phrase, முந்துநின்றாரே, may mean the devotees stand ahead of all others, or that they alone came forward to speak.

2627.reading: As a cow seeks and calls its calf, I, as a calf, sought and called my Lord; and the hidden meaning of the Vedas, who stood beyond the heavens, sought me out, came and entered into this body of flesh.
2627.nuance: The image turns: the poet calls as a calf, but the Lord comes searching like the cow. வான்கன்றுக்கு அப்பால் and ஊன்கன்றால் are unclear; கன்று may be repeated for the wordplay, the second perhaps 'the calf in flesh', the poet.

2628.reading: In bondage there is no task of one's own, since one is born into it; in release there is no task of one's own, by its nature; since the Father gives both through grace, those caught in devotion have nothing to do.
2628.nuance: பெத்தம் and முத்தம் are the Siddhanta terms for the soul's bound and released states. தன்பணி (one's own work) is traditionally taken to mean that the soul is not the agent of either; whether this rules out effort or only claims of merit is not settled by the verse.

2629.reading: Climbing the cool mountain where the hill-folk shout, with honey-laden flowers, my mind will praise none as God but Nandi, whose body bears the serpent.
2629.nuance: Line 1, பறவையிற் கற்பமும் பாம்புமெய் யாக, is obscure: கற்பம் may be the kalpa tree, an elixir or an age, and பாம்பு மெய்யாக may mean the serpent on his body or the body as serpent in a yogic reading. The mountain may be Kailasa or a hill shrine.

2630.reading: Make Nandi, the close companion, the Lord of the gods, your support and cut off birth and be saved; when one makes him close support and thinks on Siva's feet, he stands as one's support, as fire.
2630.nuance: The verse runs on துணை (support, companion) four times. அங்கியாகி (as fire) may be the inner fire of yoga or the fire that burns away bonds.

2631.reading: The Lord who destroyed the three cities of the demons who oppressed the gods: calling him the forest-dweller and the one of the dark mountain, thinking of him within the flesh, they became one with him.
2631.nuance: The famous deed (the burning of the three cities) and the homely names (கானவன், கருவரையான்) are both ways of naming him; the union comes from thinking of him inside the body (ஊனதனுள்).

2632.reading: My heart wavers as it seeks the Leader who first made both what endures and what perishes; in the mountain, in the sky, outside, in the forge and in the heart, I stood immersed.
2632.nuance: தயங்கும் can mean wavers or shines. The list of places may be where the poet searched or where he finds himself immersed in the Lord; உலை (forge) is unexpected and may be the body's inner fire.

source_issues: 2624: line 2 reads அடினையும், probably a misprint for அடிமையும்.
2626: line 2 begins ற்த்தன், a garbled division of என்றத்தன் (என்று அத்தன்).
2628: line 4 reads பத்திப்பட் டோ ர்க்குப் with a stray space inside டோர்.
2629: line 1 ends யாகப் before குறவஞ், where the sandhi should give யாகக்; line 1 is obscure.
